messages:
maria: FYI - started seeing steady KV memory growth during long-chat workloads (100k+ tokens). Not a single spike, just residency creeping up over the session. sample run: kv_residency_bytes_total ~ 3.2e9 -> 3.7e9 over ~45 minutes.

aj: ugh, that's the long-context regression we feared. Any eviction counters incrementing?

maria: eviction_count_total increments, but at a much lower rate than expected given the bytes growth. hit_rate is ~0.88 stable but reuse patterns look weird (frags not being reused).

perf-bot: automated alert: kv_residency_growth_rate > 10MB/min for 30m on model: redwood-13b-opt (canary pool).

simon: could be fragmentation / partial page retention. We should increase sampling for residency by model+host and add an eviction-age histogram. Quick query we used locally: 
```
-- prometheus-ish
avg_over_time(kv_residency_bytes_total{model=~"redwood-.*"}[10m]) by (model)
sum(increase(kv_eviction_count_total[10m])) by (model,host)
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(kv_eviction_age_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le,model))
```

lena: +1 to histogram. Also log a small kv-frag-sample snapshot on the node when residency delta > threshold. We can use a lightweight sampler to avoid OOM. Example sampler config: 
```
kv_sampler:
  enabled: true
  sample_rate: 0.005  # 0.5% of allocations
  trigger_threshold_bytes: 50_000_000
  dump_path: /var/tmp/kv-frag-samples/
```

aj: low sample_rate is good. We should also track "resident_fragment_count" and "largest_fragment_bytes" per model/host. Those two helped us catch a similar issue last year.

infra: I ran heap-profiler on one canary node and saw a lot of ~64KB fragments held because the LRU logic doesn't coalesce small evictions when paging is active. Dump excerpt: 
```
# /var/log/kv/pager-dump.log
fragment: id=0x7f9a size=65536 age=124s model=redwood-13b-opt reused=false
fragment: id=0x7f9b size=65536 age=119s model=redwood-13b-opt reused=false
... repeated patterns
```

maria: that matches the reuse=false pattern. Is kernel selection / batching relevant? We saw higher fragmentation when throughput increased (more small batches).

simon: yes — smaller batch kernels allocate more tiny KV blocks and our paging threshold isn't batching them into larger reclaimable buckets. Two follow-ups: 1) adjust pager to coalesce adjacent free frags every N evictions, 2) tweak batching heuristic to prefer slightly larger micro-batches for long-context flows.

lena: for dashboards: add panels for: "kv_residency_bytes_total by model", "resident_fragment_count by model", "largest_fragment_bytes", "kv_eviction_count_total rate", "kv_eviction_age P50/P90/P99" and a heatmap of residency delta over session length. Also add an alert on sustained residency growth (>15MB/min) with suppressed noise for <10m.

aj: can we add a synthesized metric: kv_effective_hit_rate = kv_hit_bytes / (kv_hit_bytes + kv_miss_bytes + kv_eviction_bytes) — captures evictions as a penalty.

perf-bot: new metric proposal recorded: kv_effective_hit_rate. (ticket #INF-4721)

infra: plan to run a canary with higher coalesce window and sampler enabled. Running deploy command: 
```
/deploy canary --pool=canary-kv --config=kv-pager-coalesce-v2.yaml
```

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled by @infra to canary-kv at 2024-11-07T16:12:08Z. Rolling 3 nodes.

maria: thanks — after canary runs, we'll collect frag samples and eviction-age histograms and update the dashboard. If coalescing helps, we can backfill a metric for "frag_reuse_rate".

simon: tiny nit: also instrument kernel-selection logs to emit when kernel choice changes mid-request; might help correlate small-batch kernels -> frag patterns.

lena: assigning dashboard work to @lena, sampler + alert to @aj, canary + profiler to @infra, triage + perf-run to @maria.

maria: ok, will run long-session replay after canary. Thanks all :pray:

aj: thanks. keep notes in INF-4721. :thumbsup:
